Conversely, severe negative shocks such as an unexpected global recession, a rapid escalation of geopolitical conflict, a major natural disaster, or significant adverse regulatory changes could trigger a downturn that pushes values below the lower end of our forecast ranges. These "tail risks" are inherently difficult to predict but represent scenarios with potentially extreme impacts.
